land.text: the north and east of the Central African Republic, from the towns seized on 10 December 2012 to the partition of the end of 2014

predecessors.note: Cliopatria has no row for the rebels; the land lies inside the Central African Republic's 1961-2023 shape.

land.text: the five prefectures of the ex-Séléka north and east still held after the government's February 2021 captures, at the disarmament and dissolution of the UPC

successors.note: The page dates the UPC and 3R disarmament agreements 11 July 2025 and says they 'disarmed and dissolved in a public ceremony'; four groups had announced their dissolution in Bangui on 4 December 2022. 3R is 'a rebel group, with no known links to Séléka or Anti-balaka' (the page): only the UPC of the two is an ex-Séléka faction. The rest of the armed groups (FPRC, MPC) are not accounted for on the page.

capitals.name: Bria
capitals.note: 'the FPRC's capital is in Bria' (undated, both the Civil War page and the Séléka article); the years are the researcher's span from the declaration of the Republic of Logone to the government's capture of Bria in February 2021 ('captured a number of strategic towns throughout February 2021, including towns of Bria, Kaga-Bandoro'). No page opened names a later seat. The Séléka article says the UPC is dominant in and around Bambari (20.6672 E, 5.762 N), which Adam 'intended' as the capital of the Republic of Logone. Coordinates are Natural Earth's.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the first rebel-held ground: 'On 10 December 2012, the rebels seized the towns of' N'Delé, Sam Ouandja and Ouadda. The page names the towns; Bamingui-Bangoran and Haute-Kotto are the researcher's reading. Drawn as the contested zone (the Central African Republic's contest events), not as held land.

correction.text: the north and east, held by the ex-Séléka groups

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'By the end of 2014, the country was de facto partitioned', the ex-Séléka groups holding 'the north and east' and, in an undated sentence, 'about 60% of the country's territory'; 'six rebel groups who together control two-thirds' on 19 December 2020. The eight prefectures cover 62 percent of the Central African Republic's cells. Held to the end of 2020; in February 2021 the government captured Bria, Kaga-Bandoro, the Bakouma sub-prefecture and Nzacko (keyframe seleka_2021).

correction.text: the five prefectures of the 2014 partition not named in the February 2021 captures (Vakaga, Bamingui-Bangoran, Ouaka, Haut-Mbomou, Basse-Kotto), still ex-Séléka ground after the February 2021 captures

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: in February 2021 the government 'captured a number of strategic towns throughout February 2021, including towns of Bria, Kaga-Bandoro, the Bakouma sub-prefecture, Nzacko', which are in Haute-Kotto, Nana-Grébizi and Mbomou, so those three prefectures leave (ledger loss, counterpart central-african-republic). The five prefectures left are the researcher's reading of what stayed ex-Séléka; the Central African Republic dossier's ledger marks them contested from February 2021 (confidence 1). The map ends in 2024; the keyframe runs to the UPC's disarmament in 2025.

ledger.note: 10 December 2012: the Séléka rebels seize their first towns. 'On 10 December 2012, the rebels seized the towns of' N'Delé, Sam Ouandja and Ouadda; the Central African Republic page: 'In November 2012, Séléka, a coalition of rebel groups, took over towns in the northern and central regions'. The two pages differ by a month; the civil war page's infobox gives 10 December 2012 as the start.

13 September 2013: Djotodia formally disbands Séléka. 'formally disbanded Séléka, which he had lost effective control of once the coalition had taken power' (the Séléka article: 'In September 2013, Michel Djotodia announced that Séléka had been dissolved'). From then the dossier is the ex-Séléka factions: 'it was not known who was in charge of Ex-Séléka factions'; the FPRC formed from an ad hoc ex-Séléka coalition on 12 July 2014, the UPC under Ali Darassa and the MPC are the other factions the page names. 3R is not one of them: 'a rebel group, with no known links to Séléka or Anti-balaka'. Same land and colour.

region.text: the north and east, held by the ex-Séléka groups

ledger.note: End of 2014: the ex-Séléka groups hold the north and east. 'By the end of 2014, the country was de facto partitioned' with the ex-Séléka groups in 'the north and east'; they 'controlled about 60% of the country's territory'. The eight prefectures are the researcher's reading.

14 December 2015: Séléka leaders declare the Republic of Logone. 'Noureddine Adam declared the autonomous Republic of Logone or Dar El Kuti' on 14 December 2015, 'intended Bambari as the capital' (MINUSCA said it would 'use force against any separatist attempt'). The page gives no territory for it beyond the capital; recorded as a change of name of the rebel entity, the land unchanged.

region.text: Haute-Kotto, Nana-Grébizi and Mbomou, the prefectures of the towns the government captured in February 2021 (Bria, Kaga-Bandoro, the Bakouma sub-prefecture and Nzacko)

ledger.note: February 2021: the government retakes Bria (the FPRC's capital), Kaga-Bandoro, the Bakouma sub-prefecture and Nzacko: 'captured a number of strategic towns throughout February 2021, including towns of Bria, Kaga-Bandoro, the Bakouma sub-prefecture, Nzacko, Bossembele, Bouar, Beloko and Bossangoa'. The page names towns; Haute-Kotto, Nana-Grébizi and Mbomou are the researcher's reading. Mirrors the Central African Republic gain.

region.text: the five prefectures still ex-Séléka after February 2021, held by the ex-Séléka groups

ledger.note: 11 July 2025: the UPC and 3R sign disarmament agreements. 'The UPC and 3R signed disarmament agreements with the government of President Touadéra' on 11 July 2025 (lead: they 'disarmed and dissolved in a public ceremony'); four groups had 'signed in Bangui an agreement announcing their dissolution' on 4 December 2022. Only the UPC is an ex-Séléka faction (3R has 'no known links to Séléka or Anti-balaka'); the FPRC and MPC are not covered on the page. After the dataset's last year (2024).

wars.name: Central African Republic Civil War

zones.text: the north and east held by the ex-Séléka groups

wars.outcome: Séléka seized the capital in March 2013; Djotodia resigned on 10 January 2014; the country was de facto partitioned by the end of 2014; the CPC offensive of 19 December 2020 was repelled at Bangui on 13 January 2021 and the government retook strategic towns in February 2021; the UPC and 3R disarmed in July 2025.
wars.note: Infobox 'Start date: 10 December 2012 ... Status: Ongoing'. Ceasefires: Libreville 11 January 2013, Brazzaville 24 July 2014, Nairobi (January 2015), Rome (June 2017); accord with 14 groups in February 2019. From February 2021 the government regained Haute-Kotto, Nana-Grébizi and Mbomou; the zone keeps the whole partition.

certainty.note: The land held is a prefecture-level reading of 'the north and east'; the pages give percentages and towns, no front lines.

notes: Rebel dossier added by af-08-g as the counterpart of the Central African Republic's contest and loss events. Séléka is a coalition, not a state: the colour agent should treat it as a rebel colour; the ex-Séléka factions named on the pages are the FPRC, the UPC and the MPC; 3R is not one of them. REPAIR after review (2026-10-24): (1) the government's February 2021 captures of Bria, Kaga-Bandoro, Bakouma sub-prefecture and Nzacko end the eight-prefecture keyframe at 2020 and leave the five-prefecture keyframe seleka_2021 (a loss of Haute-Kotto, Nana-Grébizi and Mbomou, confidence 2: the page names towns, the prefectures are the researcher's reading), and the capital Bria ends in 2021 (no page names a later seat; the UPC dominates Bambari). (2) The formal disbanding of 13 September 2013 is a rename: from then the dossier is the ex-Séléka factions. (3) The Séléka article was opened: it dates the coalition's emergence 15 September 2012 (agreement 20 August 2012) against the Civil War page's first towns of 10 December 2012; the dossier keeps December 2012, the first land held. The Wikipedia link is set to Séléka; the Wikidata id is still null (wikidata.org is unreachable). The dossier runs to 11 July 2025 (page-dated disarmament of the UPC and 3R) although the map ends in 2024; the rebel-held land is therefore drawn to the last year. 'rename' on 14 December 2015 stands for the declaration of the Republic of Logone, a claim without territory on the page. The status of the five remaining prefectures after 2021 is not on any page opened.
